R' Yochanan: [the seventh-day willow overrides Shabbat] in order to publicize that it is from the Torah
the lulav [does not override Shabbat] -- a decree on account of Rabba['s concern]
the willow -- the court's agents bring it; the lulav -- it is given over to everyone [so only the lulav needs the decree]
[the willow does not override today because] we do not know the fixing of the month
bar Hedya: [the seventh day of the willow] does not occur [on Shabbat]
Ravin and all the descenders: it does occur [that the seventh falls on Shabbat]
...and [the willow] does not override [Shabbat even in Eretz Yisrael today]
Rav Yosef: who tells us the willow is by taking? perhaps it is by standing it upright
evidently [the willow] is by taking
the mishnah: the lulav and the willow -- six or seven [days]
the mishnah: every day they circle the altar once, and on that day seven times
[the altar is circled] with the willow
[the altar is circled] with the lulav

the tosefta's incident: once the seventh fell on Shabbat; willow branches were brought on Friday and left in the courtyard; the Boethusians hid them under stones; the next day the amei ha'aretz pulled them out, and the priests brought them and stood them at the sides of the altar
for the Boethusians do not concede that beating the willow overrides Shabbat
since we [in Babylonia] do not override, they [in Eretz Yisrael] do not override either
for them too [the first day's lulav, today] does not override
all the people bring their lulavim to the Temple Mount [when the first day falls on Shabbat]
...[they bring them] to the synagogue
our earlier resolution: the Temple-Mount source is when the Temple stands, the synagogue source when it does not [so the lulav overrides Shabbat even without a Temple]
no: both are when the Temple stands -- the one in the Temple, the other in the outlying areas
the lulav, which we perform seven days in memory of the Temple
the willow, which we do not perform seven days in memory of the Temple
Rava: since a person fulfils his obligation with the willow in the lulav
Rav Zevid's Rava, version 1: the lulav is Torah law, [so] we do it seven days in memory of the Temple
version 1: the willow is rabbinic, [so] we do not do it seven days in memory of the Temple
Abba Shaul: 'willows of the brook' is written -- two: one for the lulav and one for the Temple
the willow [in the Temple] is a halakha to Moses from Sinai (R' Asi / R' Yochanan / R' Nechunya; recited again at 44a.7 and 44a.10)
the ten saplings are a halakha to Moses from Sinai
the water-libation is a halakha to Moses from Sinai
version 2: the lulav, which has a root in the Torah, is done seven days in the outlying areas in memory of the Temple; the willow, which has no root in the Torah, is not
Reish Lakish: blemished priests enter between the Ulam and the altar in order to fulfil the willow
(entertained) R' Yochanan's 'who said it?' doubts that anyone stated the willow law at all
rather: who said it is by taking -- perhaps by standing upright; who said by the blemished -- perhaps by the unblemished
the willow is an ordinance (foundation) of the prophets
the willow is a custom of the prophets
R' Abbahu, astonished a while, said: they forgot them and [the prophets] founded them again
R' Yochanan: yours say -- it is theirs (gloss-only: the text does not state whose 'theirs' is; Steinsaltz reads: the Sages')
R' Ami: the willow requires a measure
...and it is taken only by itself
...and a person does not fulfil his obligation with the willow in the lulav
Rav Chisda in R' Yitzchak's name: a person fulfils his obligation with the willow in the lulav (the bracketed words: on the first day of the festival)
Rav Nachman: [its measure is] three twigs with moist leaves
Rav Sheshet: even one leaf and one twig
rather say: even one leaf on one twig
Aivu: R' Elazar bar Tzadok took [the willow], beat it, beat it, and did not bless
Aivu and Chizkiya, Rav's grandsons, brought a willow before Rav: he beat it, beat it, and did not bless
R' Elazar bar Tzadok, asked by a man whose villagers hoe his groves and eat his olives [in the Sabbatical Year] whether that is proper: it is not proper
R' Elazar bar Tzadok: forty years I have lived in this land and not seen a man walk in paths as straight as this
his advice: declare the olives ownerless for the poor, and give coins for the hoeing of the groves
the baraita: 'you shall let it rest' -- from hoeing (Shemot 23:11)
...'and lie fallow' -- from clearing stones
Rav Ukva bar Chama: hoeing to strengthen the trees is forbidden
...hoeing to seal cracks is permitted
a person should not walk on Shabbat eves more than three parasangs
Rav Kahana (first version): we said this only of [one going] to his house; to his inn he relies on what he carries
Rav Kahana (איכא דאמרי): it was needed even for [one going to] his house
Rav Kahana: it happened to me, and I did not find even a small fried fish

objections.gloss_en: ואלא קשיא הני תרתי: דתנא חדא להר הבית ותניא אידך לבית הכנסת, ומתרצינן: כאן בזמן שבית המקדש קיים, כאן בזמן שאין -- so without a Temple the lulav is brought to the synagogue on Shabbat
